solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Pasteur unexpectedly becomes visibly emotional (5,2)

indicatorNotes.unexpectedly: the letters turn up in an order you would not expect

annotation.surface: The great scientist surprises everyone by welling up.
annotation.walkthrough: A proper name is the classic disguise for anagram fodder: Pasteur looks like the subject of the sentence, not a set of letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone who tears up has eyes filling with tears, which is being visibly emotional.

entries.clue: Primarily, trees supply paper (6)

indicatorNotes.Primarily: primarily = first of all, so take the first letter

blocks.note: to issue = to supply, as with uniforms

annotation.surface: Paper comes mostly from trees.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Primarily' reads as 'mainly' in the surface, but it only wants the first letter of the next word.
annotation.definitionFit: Tissue paper is the thin wrapping kind, so paper is the broad class and tissue one kind of it.

entries.clue: Periodically, mad Nigel hit an old Ford (6)

indicatorNotes.Periodically: at regular intervals, so every other letter

blocks.note: the even letters: mAd NiGeL hIt An

annotation.surface: An angry Nigel smashes into a vintage car.
annotation.walkthrough: The Ford Anglia was a small British family car of the 1950s and 60s, later famous as the flying car in Harry Potter.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Anglia was a small Ford family car made from 1939 to 1967.

entries.clue: Old tender of Yorkshire, Berkshire etc? (9)

annotation.definition: Old tender of Yorkshire, Berkshire etc?

blocks.note: reads as an old-fashioned carer or keeper of something
look like English counties, but both are breeds of pig

annotation.surface: Someone who used to look after English counties.
annotation.walkthrough: Yorkshire and Berkshire read as counties, but both are pig breeds; the old tender of pigs is a swineherd.
annotation.definitionFit: A swineherd was a person who looked after pigs, a job of the past.

entries.clue: Careful instruction to produce a royal portrait including son (11)

indicatorNotes.including: the phrase takes the son inside it

blocks.clueFragment: instruction to produce a royal portrait
blocks.note: PAINT A KING, what you would tell an artist to get a royal portrait

annotation.surface: Detailed guidance for commissioning a portrait of the monarch and his son.
annotation.walkthrough: The wordplay is a whole imperative sentence, PAINT A KING, run together; the S slots in after PAIN.
annotation.definitionFit: Painstaking means taking great care.

entries.clue: Young lady slurred after second drink, causing fight (8)

blocks.note: kir = white wine with blackcurrant liqueur
MISS as a drunk would say it

annotation.surface: A drunk slurring at a young woman after one drink too many starts a brawl.
annotation.walkthrough: The slurring is the drinker's own: MISS said with a drunken lisp comes out MISH.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a skirmish is a short, small-scale clash, a minor kind of fight.

entries.clue: Capsized vessels break apart (4)

indicatorNotes.Capsized: turned upside down, which in a down clue flips the word

blocks.note: reversal indicator: in a down entry an overturned word reads upwards

annotation.surface: Overturned boats break up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' and 'capsized' paint ships, but the vessels are kitchen pans.
annotation.definitionFit: A stick that snaps breaks cleanly in two, the break-apart sense of the verb.

entries.clue: Bullies close friends, stealing papers (11)

indicatorNotes.stealing: the friends take the papers into themselves

annotation.surface: A bully takes the documents of his own close friends.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bullies' reads as a plural noun but is the verb, matching INTIMIDATES.
annotation.definitionFit: To bully someone is to intimidate them.

entries.clue: Playing to him camper sort of rock (11)

indicatorNotes.Playing: the letters are played about with

annotation.surface: Performing a more flamboyant kind of rock music to him.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rock' suggests music alongside 'playing', but it is geology.
annotation.definitionFit: Metamorphic rock is one of the three main types, formed by heat and pressure.

entries.clue: Alcoholic imbibes small measure of liquid in best part of club for shots? (5,4)

annotation.definition: best part of club for shots?

indicatorNotes.imbibes: the drinker takes the other pieces inside

blocks.note: tsp = teaspoon, inside SOT after WEE

annotation.surface: A drinker knocks back a tiny measure in the best bit of the club for shots.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes the club a bar serving shots; it is a golf club, and the sweet spot is where the ball is best struck.
annotation.definitionFit: The sweet spot is the part of a club or bat that hits the ball most effectively.

entries.clue: Bachelor delivered a line regarding woman soon to be married (6)

annotation.definition: regarding woman soon to be married

blocks.note: to rid = to deliver or free, as in 'rid of'

annotation.surface: A single man gives a speech about a bride-to-be.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Delivered' suggests a speech but means freed: to be delivered from something is to be rid of it.
annotation.definitionFit: Bridal means relating to a bride, a woman about to marry.

entries.clue: Bring confidence back to Erasure’s dancing (8)

indicatorNotes.dancing: dancing letters move about, so ERASURES steps into a new order

annotation.surface: The synth-pop duo Erasure's dance music restores someone's confidence.
annotation.walkthrough: Erasure is an English pop duo; the apostrophe is ignored and the S joins the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to reassure someone is to restore their confidence, and the 're-' echoes 'back'.

entries.clue: Too much wine drunk by detectives, supporting one charged at case’s conclusion (16)

indicatorNotes.conclusion: a word's conclusion is its last letter

blocks.note: port, the fortified wine, placed by the detectives
an ion is an electrically charged particle

annotation.surface: Police drinking on the job while backing a suspect about to be charged.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One charged' sounds like a defendant, but in crosswords it is usually an ion, a charged particle.
annotation.definitionFit: Disproportionate means out of proportion, too much for the situation.

entries.clue: Washed clothes — load regularly wet, possibly? (7)

indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals, so every other letter

blocks.note: wet could be called un-dry, hence the question mark

annotation.surface: A washing load that is often left damp.
annotation.walkthrough: UNDRY is not a real word; the question mark admits the invention.
annotation.definitionFit: The washing sense: laundry means clothes and linen that are washed or due for washing.

entries.clue: Assign, if I can, to the retail banking partner (11,5)

indicatorNotes.banking: the words keep the answer as a bank keeps money

blocks.clueFragment: Assign, if I can, to the retail
blocks.note: asSIGN IF I CAN TO THE Retail

annotation.surface: Offering to transfer something to a retail bank.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Banking' reads as part of 'retail banking', but it is the instruction to find the hidden word; 'partner' sits at the end.
annotation.definitionFit: A significant other is a spouse or long-term partner.

entries.clue: Retired upper-class twit with unrestricted bank capital (6)

indicatorNotes.Retired: going back, so the letters run backwards
indicatorNotes.unrestricted: with its limits taken off, so drop the outer letters

annotation.surface: A retired toff with money in a bank that has no limits.
annotation.walkthrough: U + ASS + AN makes UASSAN, which runs backwards to NASSAU, the capital of the Bahamas.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Nassau is the capital of the Bahamas, and capital here means a capital city.

entries.clue: Cricketer and American president taking black cab with no cabbie (8)

indicatorNotes.taking: the cricketer takes the B inside

annotation.surface: A cricketer and a US president hail a London black cab that has no driver.
annotation.walkthrough: 'American president' reads as one phrase, but it splits: the A is American and the president is Xi.
annotation.definitionFit: A robotaxi is a self-driving taxi with no human driver.

entries.clue: All that is poetry following a French upstanding character (8)

indicatorNotes.following: the poetry comes after the other pieces

blocks.note: I, the letter that stands upright

annotation.surface: Poetry after a principled French figure is all there is.
annotation.walkthrough: 'All that is' looks like the start of a sentence, but it is the definition; 'upstanding character' is the letter I, a single upright stroke.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the universe takes in everything that exists, which 'all that is' describes.

entries.clue: Religious leader married friend from Paris after revolution (4)

indicatorNotes.from Paris: a word from Paris is a French word, so friend becomes AMI
indicatorNotes.after revolution: turned round, so the letters run backwards

annotation.surface: A cleric weds a French friend after an uprising.
annotation.walkthrough: M + AMI gives MAMI, which runs backwards to IMAM; 'revolution' reads as politics but means turning round.
annotation.definitionFit: An imam leads prayers in a mosque.

entries.clue: Wake communist on time, at least half-dressed? (9)

annotation.surface: Waking a communist on time, while he is only partly clothed.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: wearing trousers means your lower half, at least, is dressed, hence the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: Trousered means wearing trousers, which covers about half the body.

entries.clue: Encourage Northern Echo to plug television writer (8)

indicatorNotes.to plug: the pieces go into TV like a plug into a hole

blocks.note: Echo is E in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: Urging a regional newspaper to promote a TV writer.
annotation.walkthrough: The Northern Echo is a real newspaper in north-east England, which is what makes the split into N and E hard to see.
annotation.definitionFit: Ivan Turgenev was a Russian novelist and playwright.

entries.clue: Again considered the worth of key state reversing university probes (8)

indicatorNotes.probes: the U goes into the other letters

blocks.note: U = university, inside DEL AVER after DE

annotation.surface: An important country has its worth reassessed as a university investigates.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Key state' reads as an important nation, but key is the Del key on a keyboard; DE(U)LAVER reverses to REVALUED.
annotation.definitionFit: To revalue is to assess the worth of something again.

entries.clue: The art of copying Gaugin’s first happy error in a new way (11)

indicatorNotes.first: Gaugin's first means the first thing in Gaugin, its opening letter
indicatorNotes.in a new way: doing things in a new way means rearranging them, here the letters

blocks.note: anagram fodder, with G makes 11 letters

annotation.surface: An art forger's happy accident in copying a Gauguin.
annotation.walkthrough: The painter's name, spelt Gaugin here, is only there for its G; the art is photocopying, not painting.
annotation.definitionFit: Reprography is the reproduction of documents by photocopying and similar means.

entries.clue: When is accomplice flipping trapping snake? (8)

indicatorNotes.trapping: the words hold the answer inside them

blocks.note: read backwards: eciLPMOCCASINehW, hidden as whEN IS ACCOMplice

annotation.surface: A question about when a partner in crime will turn informer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' sounds like an accomplice turning against the gang, but it is the instruction to read backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: The water moccasin is a venomous North American snake.

entries.clue: Bartenders on Nile supply conductor (7,9)

indicatorNotes.supply: read as 'supply' the adverb of supple: bendily, so rearranged

annotation.surface: Barmen on a Nile cruise provide a guide for the tour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supply' reads as provide, but here it is supple-ly: flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Bernstein conducted the New York Philharmonic, besides composing West Side Story.

entries.clue: Cooking too much on account of celebration in Ghana’s capital (9)

indicatorNotes.capital: a word's capital is its first letter

blocks.note: over = on account of, as in 'a row over money'

annotation.surface: Food gets overcooked because of a party in Accra.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ghana's capital' tempts you towards ACCRA; it only wants the capital letter G.
annotation.definitionFit: Overdoing food means cooking it for too long.

entries.clue: A hotel reserved by artist from South Pacific island (8)

indicatorNotes.reserved by: the artist holds the A and H, as a table is held for you

blocks.note: Hotel is H in the NATO alphabet
Titian, the Venetian painter, around AH

annotation.surface: A painter books a hotel room on a Pacific island.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface nods to Gauguin, who painted in Tahiti, but the artist in the wordplay is Titian.
annotation.definitionFit: Tahitian means coming from Tahiti, an island in French Polynesia.

entries.clue: Knowing what ruler has in common with Greek mathematician? (4)

annotation.definition2: what ruler has in common with Greek mathematician?

blocks.note: knowing as in a sly, playful look

blocks.clueFragment: what ruler has in common with Greek mathematician?
blocks.note: monARCH ends with it and ARCHimedes starts with it

annotation.surface: A riddle about what a king and Archimedes share.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic riddle rather than a synonym: the letters shared by a monarch and Archimedes.
annotation.definitionFit: Arch means knowingly playful or mischievous, as in an arch smile.

entries.clue: Care worker in Beatles record (4,4)

blocks.note: to be in = to be at home
Help!, a Beatles album and single

annotation.surface: A carer appears on a Beatles album.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' reads as a linking word placing the worker in the record, but it gives HOME.
annotation.definitionFit: A home help is someone who helps elderly or ill people in their own home, a British term.

entries.clue: Clever technology cracking British Library’s security (4)

annotation.surface: AI hacks the British Library's defences.
annotation.walkthrough: The British Library really did suffer a cyber attack in 2023, which gives the surface its bite.
annotation.definitionFit: Bail is money lodged as security for an accused person's release.

entries.clue: Trick men collecting money for groups of soldiers (11)

indicatorNotes.collecting: the trick and the men gather the money between them

annotation.surface: Con men raising cash from army units.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trick men' reads as a single picture of con men, which hides that the money sits between the two pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A contingent is a group of troops forming part of a larger force.

entries.clue: Satellite seen above Washington State (4)

annotation.surface: A satellite passing over the state of Washington.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Washington State' is one place in the surface; the definition is 'State' alone, and 'seen above' places IO over WA in the down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Iowa is one of the fifty US states, in the Midwest.

entries.clue: Having people for dinner? (11)

blocks.note: taken literally, the people are the dinner itself

annotation.surface: Hosting guests for an evening meal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Having people for dinner' means entertaining guests; read literally, the people are the meal.
annotation.definitionFit: Cannibalism is eating human flesh.

entries.clue: Caught injecting drug, Republican laughed (8)

indicatorNotes.injecting: putting the drug and the R into NICKED

annotation.surface: A Republican caught taking drugs laughs it off.
annotation.walkthrough: To nicker is to snigger or neigh softly, so it can mean laughed.
annotation.definitionFit: To nicker is to give a soft, suppressed laugh.

entries.clue: Cocktail club started by society men (11)

indicatorNotes.started by: the society and men come first

blocks.note: a crew is a team of men
a driver is a golf club

annotation.surface: A cocktail club founded by a group of society gentlemen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Club' reads as a social club in the surface, but it is a golf club, the driver.
annotation.definitionFit: A screwdriver is a cocktail of vodka and orange juice.

entries.clue: To some extent, hoped a general turned traitor (8)

indicatorNotes.To some extent: only part of the words is used

blocks.note: read backwards: laRENEGADEpoh, from hoPED A GENERal

annotation.surface: A general unexpectedly switched sides.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turned traitor' is a natural phrase, but 'turned' is the reversal instruction and 'traitor' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A renegade is someone who deserts a cause, a traitor.

entries.clue: In crease, run after beating extra cover? (11)

indicatorNotes.after beating: the letters once beaten out of shape

annotation.surface: A cricket scene: a batsman safe in his crease scampers a run after the ball beats extra cover.
annotation.walkthrough: Extra cover is a fielding position in cricket, and the crease is the line a batsman must reach; the definition means extra insurance.
annotation.definitionFit: Reinsurance is insurance taken out by an insurer, a further layer of cover.

entries.clue: Home-made meal didn’t include alcohol for Spooner (6,5)

indicatorNotes.for Spooner: swap the opening sounds of the two words

blocks.note: lacked = didn't include; takes the P from the other word
punch, the mixed alcoholic drink; takes the L from the other word

annotation.surface: A sandwich lunch from home with no booze in it.
annotation.walkthrough: The Reverend Spooner swapped the starts of words; LACKED PUNCH becomes PACKED LUNCH.
annotation.definitionFit: A packed lunch is food prepared at home to eat elsewhere.

entries.clue: Churchgoer maybe cut up about sage monk lacking boundaries (11)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down entry, the word reads upwards
indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so PAER goes around the other pieces

blocks.note: to reap = to cut a crop; reversed to PAER
a rishi is a Hindu sage

annotation.surface: A churchgoer upset about a wise monk with no limits.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut up' reads as upset, but it splits: cut is the word, and up turns it round in this down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: A parishioner is a member of a parish, typically a churchgoer.

entries.clue: Irritated, state worked to remove leaders (11)

indicatorNotes.to remove leaders: take off the first letter of each word

annotation.surface: An annoyed nation acted to oust its heads.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leaders' reads as political leaders, but it means first letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: exasperated describes being irritated to the point of losing patience.

entries.clue: Thieves and southern outlaw sent the wrong way (4)

indicatorNotes.sent the wrong way: sent backwards, so the letters reverse

annotation.surface: Robbers and a Southern outlaw run off in the wrong direction.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Thieves' and 'outlaw' read as nouns; both are verbs, thieves meaning steals and outlaw meaning ban.
annotation.definitionFit: Nabs means steals, which is what someone who thieves does.

entries.clue: More dismissive of finer fish almost cooked (8)

indicatorNotes.almost: almost a fish is a fish not quite complete, so the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.cooked: the letters are cooked up into a new order

annotation.surface: A food snob sneering at fish that is not quite done.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' fits the fish in the surface, but it is the instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Sniffy means scornful, so sniffier is more dismissive.

entries.clue: Entrance French working men touring studio every so often (5,4)

indicatorNotes.every so often: every so often means at intervals, so only every other letter of studio is kept

blocks.note: on = working, as a machine is
OR = other ranks, ordinary soldiers; ON and OR go around TDO

annotation.surface: French labourers touring a studio at intervals pass through the entrance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Working men' reads as one phrase, but it is two separate pieces that wrap round the letters from studio.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a front door is the main way into a house, one kind of entrance.

entries.clue: Creative principle found in all native working (4,5)

indicatorNotes.working: the letters are worked into a new order

annotation.surface: A creative spirit shared by all local workers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Found in' looks like a hidden-word signal, but the letters are not in a row; they are an anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: Élan vital, Bergson's term, is the creative life force behind evolution.

entries.clue: Bank of Scotland supports tennis champion cycling back, partly? (9)

indicatorNotes.cycling: the first letter moves round to the end
indicatorNotes.supports: in a down entry, the bank sits below the tennis player

blocks.note: Chris EVERT with her E moved to the end
a brae is a Scottish hillside or bank

annotation.surface: A Scottish bank sponsors a former tennis champion's comeback.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bank of Scotland' reads as the bank, but it is a Scots word for a slope; 'back, partly' means pieces of the spine.
annotation.definitionFit: Vertebrae are the bones that together make up the backbone.

entries.clue: Criminal protecting my city (8)

blocks.note: a fence is a receiver of stolen goods
Lor! = my! as an exclamation, inside FENCE

annotation.surface: A criminal guarding my home town.
annotation.walkthrough: 'My' reads as a possessive but is the exclamation, like 'my!' or 'Lor!', both cries of surprise.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Florence is the Tuscan capital, one Italian city among many.

entries.clue: Atheist, bishop, priest, and US soldier overwhelmed by debts (11)

indicatorNotes.overwhelmed by: the debts engulf the other pieces

blocks.note: RR = Right Reverend, a bishop's title
Eli, the priest in the Book of Samuel
a GI is an American soldier

annotation.surface: A godless man plus a bishop, a priest and a GI, all drowning in debt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Atheist' is used as an adjective here, matching IRRELIGIOUS.
annotation.definitionFit: Irreligious means without religion, as an atheist is.

entries.clue: Persuades civil engineer to visit banker (7)

indicatorNotes.to visit: the engineer goes into the river

blocks.note: a banker is a river, something with banks; the Indus, around CE

annotation.surface: Persuading an engineer to go and see a man at the bank.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Banker' is a crossword joke: something with banks, a river.
annotation.definitionFit: To induce someone is to persuade them.

entries.clue: Spot person tackling wide defensive players (8)

indicatorNotes.tackling: taking on, so holding the W

blocks.note: w = wide, in cricket scoring; inside SEE

annotation.surface: A scout watches a player making tackles out wide in defence.
annotation.walkthrough: In football, a sweeper is a defender who plays behind the back line.
annotation.definitionFit: Sweepers are defenders who sweep up behind the defence.

entries.clue: Artist accepted by key international group of stars (6)

indicatorNotes.accepted by: taken in between the key and the I

blocks.note: Tracey Emin, the British artist, between G and I

annotation.surface: An artist joins a major global group of celebrities.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Group of stars' reads as celebrities but means a constellation.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Gemini, the Twins, is a constellation, a named group of stars.

entries.clue: Wire design ultimately magnificent (6)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: at the end, so the last letter

annotation.surface: A wire sculpture's design proves superb in the end.
annotation.walkthrough: A stylet is a fine wire used in surgery to stiffen or clear a catheter.
annotation.definitionFit: A stylet is a slender surgical wire or probe.

entries.clue: Damage the reputation of embarrassed-looking relations on record (9)

annotation.surface: Ruining the name of blushing relatives on the record.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Relations' reads as relatives, but it is sexual relations, a common crossword sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to discredit someone is to harm their good name.

entries.clue: Check report of bad weather (4)

indicatorNotes.report of: what is heard, so a word that sounds the same

annotation.surface: Looking at a forecast of poor weather.
annotation.definitionFit: A rein physically checks a horse, and to rein in means to check or restrain generally.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Check' reads as a noun in the surface, as in checking a forecast, but it is the verb, to restrain.

entries.clue: Extremely short, cheesy party? (8)

blocks.note: a fest is a festival or party

annotation.surface: A very short party with bad jokes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cheesy' reads as corny, but here it means being a cheese.
annotation.definitionFit: Superlative of brief: briefest is the most short, which 'extremely short' paraphrases.

entries.clue: Endlessly alter drape (4)

indicatorNotes.Endlessly: without either end, so drop the first and last letters

blocks.note: CHANGE without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: Changing a curtain again and again.
annotation.definitionFit: Curtains hang or drape, the same verb for letting fabric fall in folds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' takes both ends off, not just the last letter; the word to trim is CHANGE, from alter.

entries.clue: Prompting learner to give up on part of crossword in anger, essentially (6)

indicatorNotes.essentially: at its core, so the middle letter

blocks.clueFragment: learner to give up on part of crossword
blocks.note: CLUE losing L, the learner driver's plate

annotation.surface: A beginner, prompted, gives up on a crossword clue in frustration.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a solver's fury; the part of a crossword is a CLUE.
annotation.definitionFit: Cueing someone is giving them a prompt.

entries.clue: I’m pregnant, for I’ll put out — might this have prevented it? (7-5,4)

indicatorNotes.put out: the letters are put out of order

annotation.surface: A woman announcing her pregnancy and wondering what might have prevented it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put out' has a racy sense in the surface, but it signals the anagram; the whole clue tells the story.
annotation.definitionFit: The morning-after pill is emergency contraception taken after sex.

entries.clue: One who posts poet’s missing page (6)

indicatorNotes.missing: the poet's name is missing its page, so the P comes out

annotation.surface: A poet's missing page is posted.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's in poet's reads as 'is': SPENDER is missing P, leaving SENDER.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: posting a letter is sending it, so the person who posts is its sender.

entries.clue: Go ferret for disturbing jumper (4,4)

annotation.surface: Go and rummage for a sweater that has upset you.
annotation.walkthrough: A jumper is British for a sweater, which is the sense the surface plays on; the answer is an animal that jumps.
annotation.definitionFit: A tree frog is a climbing frog, and frogs are jumpers.

entries.clue: Expected lean fighter in Chicago (7)

blocks.note: to list = to lean, as a ship does

annotation.surface: A hungry-looking boxer is expected in Chicago.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In Chicago' belongs to the definition: DUELIST with one L is the American spelling of British DUELLIST.
annotation.definitionFit: A duelist is someone who fights duels.
